## What could an exchange explore?

| Topic | A question for participants to shape |
|---|---|
| Defining success | Which outcomes matter, and who decides whether they were achieved? |
| Sustaining the work | What makes staffing, training, funding and relationships durable? |
| Authority and access | Which arrangements enable stewardship on the lands that matter? |
| Evidence and monitoring | Which observations are useful to practitioners, and which miss their purposes? |
| Teaching | What can be shared with students or other communities, by whom, and under what terms? |
| Adaptation | Which lessons travel, which need substantial adaptation, and which remain place-specific? |

Cultural burning is not defined here as a generic fuel treatment. Practitioners and their communities define its purposes, meanings and appropriate ways of describing it.

## An invitation-ready planning process

1. Ask whether a proposed exchange would be useful and whom the appropriate hosts or authorities would be.
2. Agree on purpose, compensation, participant roles, recording restrictions and review of any outputs.
3. Let hosts determine the format. A field visit or practitioner demonstration is included only if invited and appropriate.
4. Produce an agreed learning record, including what should not be generalized or shared further.
